newsitem.title: JAPAN: WEEK AHEAD - Tokyo stocks seen drifting nervously.
newsitem.headline: WEEK AHEAD - Tokyo stocks seen drifting nervously.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are expected to drift nervously without clear direction this week, after the launch of Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto's new cabinet failed to provide fresh incentives last week, analysts said.

Masaaki Higashida, strategist at Nomura Securities Co Ltd, expects the Nikkei average to trade between 20,500 and 21,500 next week. "The market will nervously keep an eye on U.S. stocks, foreign investors' stance and currencies," he said.
The key 225-share Nikkei average closed at 21,201.04 on Friday, up 567.98 points from its close the previous Friday, after fluctuating widely and directionlessly.
The key index soared on Friday, but it was mainly led by technical buying linked with trading in the futures market, brokers said.
"Today's (last Friday's) rally had nothing to do with politics. The political factor is neutral (to the market) for now," said Haruyoshi Mabuchi, chief strategist at Nikko Research Center.
"The market will want to see what sort of policies the new government comes up with," he said. "And if there are no effective policies, that would discourage the market."
Brokers mostly shrugged off the re-election of Hashimoto as prime minister and the formation of a new cabinet made up of old-guard Liberal Democratic Party members.
One of Hashimoto's first moves was to announce the establishment of a body to push for various administrative reforms.
Brokers said, however, a lack of fresh faces in the line-up of the new cabinet was unlikely to turn around foreign investors' recent net selling stance.
Recent swings in currencies will also draw the attention of participants in the stock market, analysts said.

The dollar hovered slightly above 112 yen in afternoon Tokyo on Friday, after a sell-off on Thursday following remarks by an influential Finance Ministry official that suggested the slide in the yen had gone far enough.
